image_description: A close-up, slightly angled view of a vintage comic book cover titled 'MAD DOG'. The cover features psychedelic, colorful artwork with a central character in a dynamic pose, surrounded by abstract shapes and other figures. Text elements include the title, issue number ('No. 1'), price ('15¢'), and credits. The paper appears aged with some wear on the edges.

artifact_observations.location: Top left corner, below main title
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text block containing credits/writer names ('by Val Mayerik...') exhibits slight letter distortion and merging. The characters are mostly legible but lack the crisp vector sharpness of real print, showing minor AI-generated text warping.

The skin tones have a slightly 'smudged' or painterly quality that lacks the distinct line-work separation typically found in printed comics. The boundaries between color fields bleed slightly more than expected for a high-quality scan.

The green/yellow figure in the bottom right corner has indistinct anatomy. The limbs and head merge into the background without clear definition, suggesting a failure in maintaining consistent structural integrity for secondary characters.

alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'comic book' class. It passes all testable checkpoints regarding geometry, cover art style, typography, and material appearance. Failures are limited to untestable interior features (spine staples, interior panels) which is expected for a cover-only view. The visual semantics are highly accurate to the target class.

The primary issues are minor text gibberish in the credit block (letters not fully formed), slight texture smudging in the main illustration lacking crisp ink lines, and structural ambiguity in the background figures. These prevent a perfect artifact score but do not ruin the overall illusion.
